entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jangsu, the 20th monarch of Goguryeo, reigned for an extraordinary 79 years from 413 to 491 CE, marking the zenith of the northernmost Korean Three Kingdoms' power and territorial expansion. Born in 394 CE as Ko Ryon, the eldest son of the revered Gwanggaeto the Great, Jangsu inherited a formidable military and a burgeoning empire. His reign solidified Goguryeo's dominance over the Korean Peninsula and established it as a significant regional power, engaging in complex diplomatic and military maneuvers with its southern rivals, Baekje and Silla, as well as with the Northern Wei Dynasty and the Rouran Khaganate to the north.

Under Jangsu's astute leadership, Goguryeo achieved its greatest territorial extent, stretching from present-day Inner Mongolia and Manchuria deep into the Korean Peninsula. His military campaigns were particularly successful against Baekje, culminating in the capture of its capital, Hanseong (modern-day Seoul), in 475 CE. This decisive victory led to the death of King Gaero of Baekje and forced Baekje to relocate its capital southward, fundamentally altering the geopolitical landscape of the peninsula. Jangsu also strategically moved Goguryeo's capital from Guknaeseong to Pyongyang in 427 CE, a move that symbolized and facilitated his southern expansionist ambitions and reinforced Goguryeo's claim over the heart of the peninsula.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jangsu's nearly eight-decade reign solidified Goguryeo's dominance over the Korean Peninsula and established it as a major East Asian power, culminating in the capture of Baekje's capital and the relocation of his own to Pyongyang.
